* The research assistant: Answers that stream in, live progress while it searches and reads, and a citation on each claim that opens the source at the right paragraph.
* Evidence on every answer: Sources, confidence, and whether a cited judgment has since been overruled.
* The drafting editor: Citations and defined terms as live objects, formatting that follows each court's rules, and PDF and Word export that's ready to file.
* The document viewer: Long judgments in PDF or text, with the cited passage highlighted.
* Matter workspaces: Where a firm keeps its research and drafts, visible only to the people who should see them.
* Speed in real conditions: Long documents, streamed answers, mid-range laptops, and office connections that drop.
* The design system: Built with our designer, so the product looks and behaves as one thing.
* Internal tools: The software our legal, research, and operations teams run on, with the same care as the product.

**The Hard Problems You'll Take On**

* Showing uncertainty without hiding the answer: Making it visible, claim by claim, when an answer is part grounded, part inferred, or leans on an overruled judgment, without burying the lawyer in warnings.
* Making slow, fallible AI feel dependable: Show progress honestly, handle partial and failed results gracefully, and never present a half-finished answer as a finished one.
* An editor that knows what it contains: Clauses, citations, and defined terms as structured objects that can be checked and flagged when the law changes, while the lawyer still types as freely as in Word.

**What You Bring**

* You've shipped a complex web app that people use for real work, in TypeScript and React or a similar framework, and can talk through a hard architecture call you made in it
* Deep browser knowledge: you can profile a slow page, find what's blocking it, and keep a large interactive screen fast against Core Web Vitals
* Streaming and async UI: server-sent events or WebSockets, cancellation, and the error and partial states most apps skip
* Accessibility and tests are part of done for you, not a later ticket
* Comfort working with backend and research to decide what an answer must carry, so the screen can show it honestly
* Happy to be in the code, down to the empty states

**Bonus Points**

* A rich-text editor built on ProseMirror, Lexical, or similar, taken well past the default setup
* AI products: streamed model output, citations, confidence, or human-review interfaces
* Document-heavy interfaces: PDF rendering, virtualised long documents, highlights and annotations
* A design system built from zero

**This Isn't the Role If**

* You think a spinner is a finished design for a ten second wait. Most of the hard work is in the states between "loading" and "done."
* You want a mature design system to work inside. We're building it.
* You want the backend to hand you finished data.
* You want to architect and hand off.

**What You Get**

* Real ownership of frontend architecture and the code that matters most, from day one
* The chance to build a design system from zero, alongside our designer
* Work shoulder to shoulder with practising lawyers on a product built for real legal work
* A hand in making justice more accessible in one of the largest judicial systems on earth

title: Staff Frontend Engineer (Product UI and Design)
description:
****About Lexsi Labs****

Lexsi Labs is a frontier AI lab working toward aligned, interpretable and safe superintelligent systems. Our near-term mission is to build safety-aware autonomous systems for mission-critical settings such as banking, insurance, government and healthcare. We believe the institutions that deploy AI should be able to audit, correct and own the risk of the models they rely on, and we build the research and the platform that make that possible.

Our research spans AI alignment methodologies, interpretability-led system design, and foundation model research across language, structured and tabular data, and autonomous systems. We have published 25+ papers in the past 15 months across conferences including ICLR, ICML, WWW, IJCNN, MICCAI and EurIPS. Our labs are in India (Mumbai and remote), Paris and London.

We operate with a flat structure, high autonomy, and a strong bias toward engineers who take full ownership of what they build, from architecture to production behaviour.

****About the Role****

We are building the platform through which institutions own the AI they depend on. Post-training, alignment, evaluation, deployment and monitoring run inside the customer’s own environment, on the methods our labs publish.

The people using it vary widely. Post-training scientists and AI researchers run experiments at the edge of what current methods can do. AI and ML engineers take models and agents into production. Data scientists build and validate models on enterprise data. Platform and infrastructure teams operate the compute and services underneath. Inside banks, insurers and public institutions, model risk, validation and audit teams need to understand and sign off on results without writing code, and business owners need to see what is running and how it is performing. The same screen often has to serve a researcher and a risk reviewer.

The interface decides whether frontier model science stays in research papers or becomes something every institution can operate.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will write production React and TypeScript most of the week, own the frontend architecture of the platform, and make the final call on its flows, information architecture and visual design. You will work with a product designer and one or two frontend engineers, setting the standard through code and review rather than management. Expect roughly 70% of your time on building and 30% on design decisions, review and direction.

****What you’ll work on****

* Own the frontend architecture of a large React and TypeScript application: routing and layout, code splitting, state boundaries, and the contracts between the UI and backend services.
* Own the component library and design tokens as a single system used across the application, evolving it incrementally in a live codebase without pausing feature work.
* Design and build data-dense interfaces: virtualised tables over large result sets, live metrics and log streams, trace and graph visualisations, side-by-side comparisons, and code and configuration editors.
* Build a real-time data layer over SSE and WebSockets with reconnection, backpressure and cache semantics that stay consistent with request-response queries.
* Build schema-driven form systems for deeply nested, conditional configuration, validated against backend schemas.
* Design interfaces that work for users with very different levels of technical depth, from researchers to risk reviewers, without splitting the product in two.
* Make the final call on information architecture, interaction and visual design, and take your decisions from Figma to production yourself.
* Set and enforce performance budgets: render profiling, bundle size, and interaction latency on locked-down enterprise machines.
* Ship builds that run in restricted and fully offline networks, with reproducible builds, self-hosted assets and no runtime dependence on external hosts.
* Meet enterprise requirements in the UI: SSO, role-aware interfaces, auditability, accessibility, and internationalisation including right-to-left layouts.
* Raise the engineering bar across the frontend: type safety, testing strategy, tooling and code review.
* Work directly with researchers and platform engineers to turn new methods into usable product, often before the method has settled.

****You may be a good fit if you have****

* 8+ years building production web applications, including several years as the technical lead on a complex product UI.
* Expert-level TypeScript and React, including React 19 rendering and concurrency behaviour and hands-on performance profiling.
* Owned the architecture of a large frontend codebase and improved it materially while the team kept shipping.
* Led an incremental migration in a live application, such as a component library, state management approach, router or build system.
* Built interfaces where performance was the hard problem: tens of thousands of rows, high-frequency streaming updates, large JSON or log payloads, or complex interactive charts.
* Deep, practical experience with TanStack Query or equivalent, Tailwind CSS, React Hook Form with Zod, Vite and pnpm.
* Built or maintained a design system with tokens, theming, accessibility to WCAG standards and documentation in Storybook.
* Designed and shipped product yourself, with a portfolio that shows both the decisions you made and the code that implemented them.
* Built for multiple user types with different expertise in the same product, and made it work for each of them.
* A testing discipline built on Vitest or Jest, Playwright and API mocking.
* Worked without a product manager or a full spec, decided what to build, and defended the decision with evidence.
* Clear written and verbal communication of trade-offs to engineers, researchers and leadership.

****Strong candidates may also have****

* Built developer tools or ML tooling, such as experiment tracking, training dashboards, evaluation or observability products.
* Visualisation depth with ECharts, D3, or canvas and WebGL rendering.
* Built graph or trace viewers (React Flow or similar) and embedded code editors (CodeMirror or Monaco).
* Shipped software into on-premise, regulated or air-gapped environments.
* Built right-to-left and multi-locale products.
* Used state machines such as XState for complex multi-step flows.
* Instrumented frontends with OpenTelemetry and web vitals.
* Shipped LLM-powered product features.
* Contributed to open-source frontend libraries.

If you meet most of this but not all, we would still like to hear from you.

****What this role is not****

* Not a people management role at the start. There are no direct reports, and influence comes through code, review and design decisions.
* Not a visual design role. You will design, but you will be measured on what ships to production.
* Not a ticket-implementation role. You will be expected to question specs and decide what should be built.

****What we expect in the first six months****

* Own a set of redesigned core flows end to end, from information architecture through to production.
* Establish the component system and tokens as the single source of truth for the application.
* Set performance budgets for the heaviest views and bring them within budget.
* Put test coverage in place across the core flows.

****How we will evaluate****

* A review of shipped work where you can show both the design decisions and the code.
* A build exercise on a data-dense screen, assessed on code quality, structure and performance.
* A design critique of a flow in our product, where you decide what changes and why.
* An architecture conversation on component systems, data and streaming layers, and offline deployment.

**About the Role**

We are looking for an experienced API Integration Engineer with strong expertise in REST APIs, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and web technologies. The ideal candidate will help clients integrate APIs into their existing systems, understand their technical requirements, and recommend efficient, scalable, and reliable implementation approaches.

The candidate should have a deep understanding of how APIs work, hands-on experience with frontend and/or backend technologies, and the ability to troubleshoot integration challenges and optimize the way APIs and external scripts are implemented within web applications.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Work with clients to understand their technical requirements and help integrate APIs with their existing applications, websites, and backend systems.
* Analyze API documentation and translate business and technical requirements into practical implementation approaches.
* Implement, test, debug, and troubleshoot REST API integrations across different systems.
* Work with HTTP requests and responses, JSON payloads, headers, query parameters, status codes, and API error handling.
* Develop and troubleshoot web integrations using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
* Optimize the loading and execution of JavaScript files and third-party scripts to minimize their impact on website performance.
* Identify opportunities to improve API integration efficiency, reduce unnecessary network requests, and optimize request-response handling.
* Diagnose integration issues using browser developer tools, network inspection, server logs, and API testing tools.
* Collaborate with client technical teams and internal engineering teams to resolve implementation challenges.
* Provide technical guidance on API usage, integration workflows, implementation dependencies, and best practices.
* Test integrations across different environments and ensure functionality, reliability, and compatibility with existing systems.
* Document implementation steps, troubleshooting procedures, and recommendations for future integrations.

**Required Skills and Qualifications**

* Minimum 4+ years of hands-on experience in API integration, web development, or a related software engineering role.
* Strong understanding of REST APIs, HTTP/HTTPS protocols, request-response lifecycles, HTTP methods, status codes, headers, JSON, and error handling.
* Strong proficiency in JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
* Practical experience integrating APIs with frontend applications, backend services, or third-party platforms.
* Understanding of JavaScript execution, asynchronous operations, Promises, async/await, and dynamic script loading.
* Hands-on experience optimizing script loading using techniques such as async, defer, and dynamic script injection.
* Proficiency in using Postman or similar tools for API testing and debugging.
* Experience using browser developer tools to inspect network requests, debug JavaScript issues, and identify performance bottlenecks.
* Understanding of CORS, browser behavior, cookies, caching, and common web integration challenges.
* Experience working with at least one frontend or backend technology, such as React, Angular, Vue.js, Node.js, Python, or Go.
* Strong analytical, troubleshooting, communication, and problem-solving skills.

**Good to Have**

* Experience integrating third-party JavaScript libraries, SDKs, widgets, and external services into client websites.
* Experience working directly with clients on technical implementations and integration troubleshooting.
* Understanding of website performance optimization, browser rendering, lazy loading, and reducing render-blocking resources.
* Experience interpreting technical documentation and independently developing integration solutions.
* Ability to assess different implementation approaches and recommend the most efficient solution based on the client's existing architecture.

**Ideal Candidate Profile**

* Has a deep, practical understanding of APIs and can explain how to integrate them efficiently into different systems.
* Can independently review API documentation, identify dependencies, and implement integrations with minimal supervision.
* Understands how JavaScript scripts are loaded and executed in browsers and how they affect website performance.
* Can identify the root cause of API failures, integration conflicts, and performance issues.
* Is comfortable communicating with clients, understanding their technical environments, and guiding them through implementation.
* Can balance functionality, performance, maintainability, and compatibility when recommending integration approaches.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.
  
  
Join EY and help to build a better working world.

Global Delivery Services refers to EY's worldwide network of service delivery centers. The GDS team plays an important role in EY’s strategy by ensuring effective support to EY’s growth agenda.
  
  
Our journey started in 2002 with approximately 200 people. Today we stand at 80,000+ professionals in ten locations around the world. We operate in Argentina, China, Hungary, India, Philippines, Poland, Sri Lanka, Mexico, Spain and the United Kingdom.
  
  
Client service is focused on providing Consulting, Assurance, Tax, Strategy & Transactions, and Knowledge support to our clients around the world. The teams enable account teams worldwide to provide seamless, high-quality, value-added support, helping deliver exceptional client service.

Markets, BMC, AWS, Finance and Accounting, Risk Management, Procurement, People Shared Services, IT Service Delivery and IT Global Infrastructure services, are among the services offered by Enablement Services.
  
  
Our innovation specialists serve the GDS Client Service and Enablement Services teams, along with Service Lines, Core Business Services and Sectors. The team brings the desired environment, technologies and skilled teams together for facilitation, rapid prototyping and innovative thinking. The competencies offered include analytics, digital, user experience, mobile technology, infrastructure, Microsoft technologies and open innovation.

We are seeking an experienced Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM Lead / Senior Consultant to design, deliver, and optimize enterprise-grade D365 and Power Platform solutions. This role combines deep technical expertise with solution ownership, team leadership, and stakeholder engagement to drive business outcomes across complex CRM environments.

* Oversee system architecture, performance tuning, testing, troubleshooting, and deployment to ensure optimal functionality and user experience.

* Engage with business and technical stakeholders, translating complex technical concepts into clear and actionable discussions.

* Strong expertise in Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM configuration, customization, and solution delivery.
* Proficiency in C#, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS with hands-on experience in plugins and workflows.
* Solid knowledge of Power Platform including Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI.
* Strong understanding of CRM data models, security, and business processes.

At EY, we’ll develop you with future-focused skills and equip you with world-class experiences. We’ll empower you in a flexible environment, and fuel you and your extraordinary talents in a diverse and inclusive culture of globally connected teams. Learn more.

Our dedication is to cultivate EY into an environment where diverse perspectives are celebrated, creating a supportive atmosphere for individuals to authentically be themselves and contribute their utmost.

Our shared values include integrity, respect, teaming, inclusiveness, energy, enthusiasm, courage to lead, and building relationships based on doing the right thing.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Forward-Deployed Engineer / AI Product Manager

Tuning Research · India (hybrid, at client sites)

About Tuning Research

Tuning Research is an applied AI engineering company, founded by IIT Kanpur alumni, that builds production-grade agentic AI systems for enterprises. We’re a 20-person team that works as an extended AI team for our clients across knowledge and documents, business operations, video intelligence, voice AI and marketing automation.

About the role

We’re hiring a Forward-Deployed AI Product Manager to own client transformations end to end: scope it, design it, build parts of it, ship it, and get it used.

You’ll be the one person from Tuning Research who lives inside the client’s business. Typically that’s a mid-to-large Indian enterprise replacing spreadsheets and legacy systems (HRMS, ERP, accounts, operations) with AI-native software. You sit with their teams, work out what should be built, design it, build and ship parts of it yourself, and make sure hundreds of people actually use it. A small remote team of AI, full-stack and mobile engineers works with you, and our founders stay closely involved.

The title says product manager, but the job is closer to a forward-deployed engineer: half product, half engineering, all of it on the customer’s ground.

What a week looks like

* Monday: At the client’s office. Stand-ups with business teams to agree priorities and blockers.
* Tuesday: Building. Backend endpoints, data migration scripts, an AI extraction flow, or a Figma screen.
* Wednesday: On the floor or at a site. Watch people use what shipped, demo it, capture what’s wrong.
* Thursday: Review the engineers’ code, test on real data, deploy, and fix what breaks.
* Friday: Write next week’s specs, then review with our founders and client leadership.

What you’ll do

*Scope the right thing*

* Run discovery across departments and map how work, material and money actually flow.
* Separate what people ask for from what they need. Decide what is configuration, what is a one-off, and what becomes a product feature.
* Turn findings into a prioritised monthly scope with clear acceptance criteria, and say no to things that would fragment the platform.

*Own the client relationship*

* Be the single point of contact for everyone from frontline supervisors to the MD.
* Run weekly working sessions, fortnightly reviews and monthly scope meetings, and keep one tracker of every request and decision.
* Explain trade-offs, delays and risks plainly, before they become surprises.

*Design the system*

* Own the system design: the data model, integrations with existing ERPs and accounting systems, and roles and permissions.
* Decide where AI belongs (document reading, matching, alerts, copilots) and where plain software is enough.

*Build, verify and deploy*

* Write backend code yourself: APIs, integrations, and data migration from Excel and legacy systems.
* Review every pull request from your engineers, and test on the client’s real data before anything ships.
* Run releases and own incidents and fixes in production.
* Set up evals for AI features so accuracy is measured, not assumed.

*Design the experience and drive adoption*

* Design screens in Figma for people who don’t type much: offline-first, in Hindi and English, for low-cost Android phones.
* Test designs with real users before the team builds them. Train users and write simple guides.
* Watch usage, find where people drop off, and fix it.

What you need

* 3–6 years building and shipping software, including at least 2 years in a client-facing, founding-engineer, product-engineer or forward-deployed role.
* Strong backend skills in Python or TypeScript/Node: REST APIs, PostgreSQL or similar, and SQL you write yourself.
* Hands-on experience with LLM applications: prompt design, document extraction, retrieval, tool-calling agents, and evaluating output quality.
* Able to read, review and reject code. Comfortable with Git, CI/CD, Docker and one cloud (AWS, GCP or Azure).
* Product sense: you can write a clear spec, prioritise with explicit trade-offs, and design a usable screen in Figma.
* Able to run a workshop with a site supervisor in the morning and an MD in the afternoon, and you write plainly.
* Fluent Hindi and English.
* Willing to work from client offices and travel to sites, daily in the first month or two of an engagement.

Nice to have

* You’ve built ERP, HRMS, accounting or operations software, or you know Tally, GST, TDS or payroll.
* Experience with construction, infrastructure, manufacturing or field-operations businesses.
* You’ve shipped a mobile app (React Native or Flutter), ideally offline-first.
* You’ve led data migration from Excel and legacy systems.
* You speak a regional Indian language beyond Hindi.

Who succeeds here

You have high agency and low ego, and you’re comfortable when the plan changes. You’ve shipped something real, whether at a startup, a hackathon or on an on-call rotation, and you’d rather fix the problem than write about it. You stay calm while a client watches you fix something live.

Work setup

* Location: Hybrid, at client offices in India. Daily for roughly the first 1–2 months of an engagement, then about 3 days a week.
* Travel: Regular visits to client sites.
* Team: You lead a remote AI engineer, full-stack engineer and mobile engineer.
* Reports to: Tuning Research founders.
* Engagements: Typically 12-month programmes, with the chance to roll out across the client’s group companies.

What success looks like

* 30 days: You’ve met every department and mapped how work and money move. The first monthly plan is agreed and the build is under way.
* 90 days: The first module is in use at pilot sites, the engineers ship every week, and the key build-vs-integrate decisions are made with the client.
* 6 months: Core modules are live and client leadership treats you as part of their team.
* 12 months: One platform runs the client’s core operations, and leadership sees the numbers daily.

How we hire

1. Intro call (30 min): Your background and why this role.
2. Discovery role-play (60 min): One of us plays a client’s department head describing a messy problem. You run the conversation and play back what you’d build.
3. Take-home (one weekend): Build a small API that uses an LLM to extract a real-world business document into structured fields. Add a one-page spec and one Figma screen for the end user.
4. Code and design review (60 min): Walk us through the take-home, and we review a pull request together.
5. Founders’ conversation: Working style, travel and expectations.
